newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Lower taxes, better demand lift Hoogovens in H2 96.
newsitem.headline: Lower taxes, better demand lift Hoogovens in H2 96.

text.p: Hoogovens NV said on Thursday a combination of lower taxes and stronger demand for its products had enabled it to post higher than expected profits in the second half of 1996.

"Market demand in volume terms increased both for steel and aluminium in the second half of the year, but this led only to a very limited improvement in prices," chairman Maarten van Veen told a news conference on the company's 1996 results.
Lower taxes were also a factor behind a second-half performance which exceeded the company's own forecast and that of most investment analysts.
Taxes claimed only 24 percent of Hoogovens' profits in 1996, compared with 35 percent in 1995.
Van Veen said this was due in part to a conservative policy in the past under which Hoogovens had put more money aside than necessary to meet its tax liabilities.
Hoogovens had said as late as last November that second-half net profit from ordinary activities would roughly match the equivalent first-half figure of 142 million guilders.
Analysts had forecast a full-year net profit range of 260 to 310 million guilders, but 1996 results published on Thursday showed net profit from ordinary activities of 325 million.
